evidence_items.explanation: Record acquisition activity shows continuing demand for SaaS assets and functioning exit channels. Acquisition volume alone does not establish operating health or disprove a developing business-model failure.

evidence_items.publisher: Bain & Company, distributed by PR Newswire
evidence_items.locator: Section 'Fund-raising falls for a fourth consecutive year as competition for capital further intensifies'
evidence_items.explanation: Bain documents a fourth year of fundraising pressure and distributions equal to only 14% of net asset value. It also reports rising buyout and exit values and slightly positive net cash flow, leaving a picture of serious strain rather than a demonstrated industry-wide breakdown.

evidence_items.publisher: National Venture Capital Association, using PitchBook data
evidence_items.locator: Key Findings, paragraph introducing venture-backed exits
evidence_items.explanation: The release documents weak distributions, concentrated fundraising and sharply reduced first-time fund formation, alongside strong investment and increased exit value. Those observations support concern about capital recycling but do not establish failure of the whole VC business model.

evidence_items.publisher: Reuters, syndicated by American Journal of Transportation
evidence_items.explanation: The report establishes a severe contemporary valuation decline. Its index includes businesses beyond SaaS, and market-value losses do not measure whether subscription businesses can operate sustainably.

unresolved_gaps: No stated threshold distinguishes 'collapse' from severe but survivable industry strain.
The retained evidence does not jointly measure representative SaaS operating viability and VC/PE realized returns across the target period.
Deal and exit values do not reveal how much cash investors actually recovered or whether typical funds earned sustainable returns.
The evidence spans different geographic populations and cannot establish a universal industry outcome.
